items.toString: [Doc] Document exclusive NTP sources option (ntp_sources field) - BE

The backend now supports a new ntp\_sources field that allows users to specify exclusive NTP servers. When set, only the user's specified servers are used — no default pool or auto\-discovered sources are included, from discovery through installation. This is mutually exclusive with the existing additional\_ntp\_source field.

The main use case is air\-gapped and security\-sensitive environments where the default public NTP pool is unreachable or not permitted.

{{Description needs finalizing:}}

{{api-int.<cluster_name>.<base_domain>}} is the internal API endpoint for OCP. It is required whenever DNS is required. This means that it is always required for User Managed Networking.

It appears in the example in section 2.4.1.`However, it is not mentioned in section 2.4.2 External DNS reqirements and needs to be added.

Section to be updated: [https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/assisted_installer_for_openshift_container_platform/2026/html-single/installing_openshift_container_platform_with_the_assisted_installer/index#external-dns-requirements_prerequisites]

Add the highlighted bullet below and possibly the note (needs verification):
h3. 2.4.2. External DNS

Installing multi-node cluster with user-managed networking requires external DNS. External DNS is not required to install multi-node clusters with cluster-managed networking or Single-node OpenShift with the Assisted Installer. Configure external DNS after installation to connect to the cluster from an external source.

External DNS requires the creation of the following record types:
 * A/AAAA record for {{{}api.<cluster_name>.<base_domain>{}}}.

 * *A/AAAA record for {{{}api-int.<cluster_name>.<base_domain>{}}}.* 

 * A/AAAA record with a wildcard for {{{}*.apps.<cluster_name>.<base_domain>{}}}.

 * A/AAAA record for each node in the cluster.

{quote}{color:#172b4d}*Note: The {{api-int}} record is required for internal cluster communication and is validated by the Assisted Installer during the pre-installation phase for clusters using User-Managed Networking (UMN). /* {*}Required for internal cluster communication and installation in user-managed networking environments).{*}{*}{*}{color}
{quote}
*Important* Do not create a wildcard, such as {{{}*.<cluster_name>.<base_domain>{}}}, or the installation will not proceed. A/AAAA record settings at top-level domain registrars can take significant time to update. Ensure the newly created DNS Records are resolving before installation to prevent installation delays. For DNS record examples, see Example DNS configuration.

Link to Slack thread: [https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/CUPJTHQ5P/p1768989209470999?thread_ts=1768989207.100219&cid=CUPJTHQ5P]

*What stage of the user journey are you targeting?*

Hint: Choose from Discover, Learn, Try, Adopt, Expand

[Answer]

*Why is this content important?*

Hint: Provide a brief summary of how of this content will impact the end user

[Answer]

*What is the main user goal aka job to be done?*

Hints:
 * Phrase the job to be done in the following way: “As a [persona] I want to [goal] so that I can [result].”

 * Seek additional input from customer facing team for their perspective
 * Tie this user goal to a real world situation. Base the goal around the impact to the user, not so much based around the feature itself.

[Answer]

*What high level steps does the user need to take to accomplish the goal?*

Hint: Provide a general outline of the steps needed.
 # [Step]

*(Optional) What is the general sentiment of users towards this goal?*

When installing OpenShift on *vSphere using the Assisted Installer*, the installation flow does *not* create MachineSets or Machines automatically.
This is expected behavior, but currently *not documented anywhere in our official docs*, and customers may run into issues when trying to scale their cluster or add worker nodes later.

We created an internal step-by-step guide that documents:

* The missing conceptual note that Assisted Installer *does not create MachineSets* for vSphere installs.
* Required *post-install vSphere configuration* (cloud provider integration must be completed before Machine API works).
* How to create a *clean RHCOS OVA-based template* properly.
* How to build a *vSphere MachineSet YAML* (with placeholder explanation).
* How to validate the MachineSet, monitor Machine lifecycle, and confirm node join.
* Scaling (manual & autoscaling) instructions.
* Trouble-shooting for typical failure cases.

This content would significantly help customers and reduce support load.

The guide PR is not merged yet and can be found here [https://github.com/openshift/assisted-service/pull/8441.|https://github.com/openshift/assisted-service/pull/8441.]{*}{*}
